M_1_SQRTPI 0.564189583547756286948\n#endif\n\nenum OptionType {\n    CALL = 0,\n    PUT = 1\n};\n\nstruct OptionInput {\n    int type;           // CALL or PUT\n    double strike;      // Strike {\n    return M_1_SQRTPI * M_SQRT1_2 * exp(-0.5 * x * x);\n}\n\n// Black-Scholes formula for European options\ndouble blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    const double S = {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfy6vXiM4nDXokJHjEx16","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The benchmark now prices options on the GPU in CUDA, and the executable is still `black_scholes`. The build is clean with no warnings, and it passes `-v` at every size I tried (0, 1, 7, 10, 11, 257, 100000).\n\n**Changes (only `black-scholes/black_scholes.cpp` and `black-scholes/CMakeLists.txt`):**\n- **Kernel:** one thread per option, with a grid-stride loop so any `-n` works. The pricing math (`blackScholes`, `cumulativeNormal`) is unchanged, now marked `__host__ __device__`.\n- **Option generation on the device:** each option is a pure function of its index, so the kernel generates its own input and the host no longer uploads a 72-byte struct per option. The host builds only the first ≤10 options that validation checks.\n- **Timing:** the timer covers device allocation, the upload of the 7-entry test table, the kernel, and the result download. The CUDA context is created before the timer starts, so driver startup isn't counted.\n- **No CPU fallback:** the program exits with an error if no CUDA device is present.\n- **CMake:** project languages are now CXX and CUDA, the minimum version is 3.24 (required for `native` architectures), and `black_scholes.cpp` is compiled with nvcc. Host flags (`-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra`) pass through `-Xcompiler`. `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` defaults to `native`; on a machine with no GPU at configure time, set it explicitly.\n\n**Results (RTX 3090, steady state, \"Computation time\"):**\n\n| n | CPU (original) | GPU (new) | Speedup |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 10,000 | 0.92 ms | 0.88 ms | ~1× |\n| 1,000,000 | 90 ms | 6.8 ms | ~13× |\n| 10,000,000 | 898 ms | 58.6 ms | ~15× |\n| 100,000,000 | 9,132 ms | ~450–560 ms | ~17× |\n\nAt n=10,000 the work is too small to hide launch and transfer latency, so the GPU only matches the CPU there. The large-n speedups are what the parallel version is for.\n\n**Numerical equivalence:** At n=10000, the `Sum`, `Min`, `Max`, and samples match the original to about 1e-14 relative error. The `Hash` line changes (`a1819ec14da95077` → `5b4a8471c75c4875`) because the device `erf`/`exp`/`log` aren't bit-identical to glibc. The printed prices are equivalent, but a bit-exact hash comparison against the old output will fail.\n\n**Notes:**\n- The first GPU run after a fresh build measured 69 ms once; later runs were steady, which I attribute to one-time loading. I didn't reproduce it again.\n- Remaining cost at very large n is mainly the device-to-host copy of the result array (8 bytes per option), which `-r` and validation need in full."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1114,"cache_read_input_tokens":46226,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1114},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f5fc2b75-8cec-4c57-b801-0413df796cc0","uuid":"ca9e4438-7f91-4a8f-92e1-d5e832718b1e","timestamp":"2026-10-12T22:06:26.724Z","request_id":"req_011Cfy6vXMmnhmWjkY3eBpZM"}
